title: HyTiS: Hybrid Tile Scheduling for GPU GEMM with Enhanced Wave Utilization and Cache Locality
problem: Wave quantization problem in modern large-core-count GPUs with large tile sizes causes partial wave under-utilization and degraded GEMM performance despite high peak throughput.
motivation: GEMM is fundamental to deep learning and scientific computing; modern GPUs scale cores and tile sizes, exacerbating wave quantization; existing solutions are inefficient or introduce synchronization overhead.
method: Two-level hybrid tile scheduling: Level 1 maximizes full-wave throughput via standard tiling; Level 2 reduces partial-wave latency via fine-grained adaptive tiling. Offline profiling creates micro-kernel library. L2 cache-aware tile layout selection via analytical model optimizes global-to-L2 data movement.
key_novelty: First framework to jointly address wave quantization and L2 cache affinity in GEMM; fine-grained adaptive tiling for partial waves; analytical cache model for tile layout selection.
contributions: Two-level hybrid tile scheduling framework for full and partial waves
Offline profiling to build efficient runtime search space
Analytical L2 cache model for tile layout optimization
limitations: Evaluation focused on dense GEMM; applicability to sparse or batched GEMM not discussed; tuning overhead for new architectures.
primary_theme: GEMM optimization for modern high-core-count GPUs
